values: Bar position: high bar rests on upper traps; low bar sits across rear delts. Use high bar as default.
Unrack with a full breath into the belly. Brace before you step back, not after.
Feet shoulder-width or slightly wider; toes out 20–30 degrees. Stance is individual — find yours.
Descend by sitting between the knees, not by pushing the butt back first. Elbows stay under the bar.
Depth: crease of the hip at or below the top of the knee. No partial reps.
Drive out of the hole through the whole foot. Think "spread the floor" not just "push up."
On the way up, hips and shoulders rise at the same rate — don't let the hips shoot up first.

Tier 30–39 barbell target: 1.25× BW (250 lb at 200 lb bodyweight). Re-establish current capacity in weeks 1–3 using conservative loads (RPE 6–7, 3–5 sets of 5 reps). Run working sets through Brzycki to estimate 1RM once form is solid. Powerbuilding split: squat on Session A days (low-rep compound), goblet squat can substitute for warm-up or accessory work. Do not squat and deadlift heavy in the same session — separate by at least one day.
Hip circles × 10, bodyweight squat × 10 (pause 2 sec at bottom), then barbell: 1 × 10 @ empty bar, 1 × 5 @ 50% working weight, 1 × 5 @ 75% working weight, then top sets.
Set up: 5 points of contact — both feet flat on floor, both glutes on bench, upper back on bench.
Grip: slightly wider than shoulder-width. Wrists stacked over elbows (not bent back).
Retract and depress scapula before unracking — "proud chest" arch. Hold this throughout the set.
Unrack with locked elbows; walk bar out over the chest before descending.
Bar path: lower to the lower chest / upper abdomen, not straight down. Slight arc.
Touch lightly at the bottom — no bounce. Tuck the elbows 45–75 degrees (not straight out, not tucked to sides).
Press along the same arc path back to lockout. Bar over wrists, wrists over elbows throughout.

Tier 30–39 target: 1.0× BW bench press (200 lb at 200 lb bodyweight). Historical PR 225 lb is ~1 year old — do not use it as a training baseline. Re-establish with conservative loads (RPE 6–7, 3–5 sets of 5 reps) over weeks 1–3. Estimate current 1RM via Brzycki from a working set of 5+ reps at RPE ≤ 8. Pair with deadlift on Session B days; avoid pressing to failure on the same day as heavy overhead work if that's added later.
Shoulder circles × 10, push-up × 5 slow tempo (3 sec down), then barbell: 1 × 10 @ empty bar, 1 × 5 @ 50% working weight, 1 × 5 @ 75% working weight, then top sets.
Bar over mid-foot (1 inch from shin). Hips hinge back to grip — do not squat down to the bar.
Grip just outside the legs. Double overhand until grip is the limiting factor, then use mixed or hook.
Before pulling: chest up ("proud chest"), lats engaged ("protect your armpits"), breath and brace.
Initiate by pushing the floor away — think leg press first, then hinge. Do not yank.
Bar stays in contact with the legs the entire pull. It should scrape the shin and drag up the thigh.
Lock out by squeezing glutes and standing tall — do not hyperextend the lumbar at the top.
Lower under control (hinge back first, then bend knees) or do a controlled drop from lockout.

Tier 30–39 target: 1.75× BW deadlift (350 lb at 200 lb bodyweight). Historical PR 255 lb is the biggest long-term strength gap. Re-establish starting at RPE 6 with conservative loads (weeks 1–3). Deadlift on Session B days only — never pair heavy squat + heavy deadlift in the same session. Fatigue cost is high (5/5): limit to 3–5 working sets, do not add excessive volume early in a block. Warm-up sets count toward total session fatigue; include them in weekly set tracking.
Hip hinge drill with dowel rod or broomstick × 10, then barbell: 1 × 5 @ 50% working weight, 1 × 3 @ 75% working weight, then top sets.
Lie on a bench or floor. DBs at chest level, elbows at ~45 degrees from torso (not flared 90).
Brace your core and press your feet into the floor.
Press the DBs up and slightly together — not straight up — to maximize pec engagement.
Control the descent for 2 seconds; do not bounce off the chest.
Floor press variation: forearms hit the floor at the bottom — shorter ROM but safer for
shoulders when no bench is available.
The DB press is the primary horizontal push for home gym setups. The Tier 30–39 target is
3× BW per hand × 8 reps (e.g., 24kg per hand for an 80kg athlete). Adjust targets to

available dumbbell increments. Sets of 6–10 are effective across strength and hypertrophy goals. If training on the floor (no bench), use dumbbell-floor-press as the substitute — it reduces shoulder stress and is equally effective for the push pattern.
Light DBs × 10 reps (focus on shoulder retraction), then moderate DBs × 5, then working weight.
Hold DBs in front of thighs, overhand grip. Stand tall — shoulders back, chest up.
Push hips back first, not down. The movement is a hinge, not a squat.
Maintain a slight knee bend throughout — do not let knees travel forward.
Lower until you feel a strong hamstring stretch (typically mid-shin). Back stays neutral.
Drive hips forward to stand — squeeze glutes at the top, don't hyperextend.

Primary hinge pattern for dumbbell setups. The 0.4× BW per hand target (Tier 30–39) means roughly 32kg per hand for an 80kg athlete — calibrate to what's available. Sets of 8–10 are the sweet spot for hamstring development; sets of 4–6 heavier build posterior chain strength. Easier on the lower back than conventional deadlift from the floor — appropriate for most injury profiles. Pair with goblet squat in the same session for a complete lower day.
Hip hinge pattern with dowel or PVC × 10, then light DB RDL × 8, then working weight.
Brace one hand and one knee on a bench or use a staggered stance.
DB hangs straight down from the shoulder, arm fully extended.
Row elbow past the hip — not out to the side. Think "put your elbow in your back pocket."
Pause briefly at the top; don't shrug the shoulder or rotate excessively.
Lower with control. Keep the core braced throughout — no twisting for momentum.

Pairs with dumbbell bench press to balance horizontal push and pull on the same session. Target 1:1 push:pull set ratio (or slightly more pull) to protect shoulder health over time. Sets of 8–12 work well. Heavier loads (5–8 reps) develop mid-back thickness. Because it's unilateral, it also trains anti-rotation core stability. Counts as a pull-pattern set in session logs (each arm = 1 set).
Scapular retractions (no weight) × 10, then light DB × 8, then working weight.
Pick up with a deadlift pattern — hinge, grip, brace, stand. Do not round to grab the floor.
Stand tall: shoulders packed down and back, chin level. Do not lean forward or tilt to either side.
Short, controlled steps — heel strike → midfoot → toe-off. Keep the hips level; do not waddle.
Breathing: small sips of air while braced. Do not fully relax the core mid-carry.
Set down with control using the same hinge pattern. Do not drop unless using bumper plates.

Carry pattern was absent from training prior to week 1 (trend: undertrained). Introduces without spike in session fatigue — low technique demand, easy to add as a finisher. Start at 22 kg/hand (~49 lb) for 30 m × 3 sets and progress load or distance weekly. Suitcase carry (one arm only) can substitute to add anti-lateral-flexion demand for core development. Do not superset with other grip-intensive exercises (pull-ups, rows) — let grip recover between.
No warm-up set needed. Grip the handles, brace, and go. Lighter first set (75% load) if needed.
Hold the dumbbell vertically at chest height, both hands cupping the top end.
Feet shoulder-width or slightly wider; toes turned out 15–30 degrees.
Brace hard before descending — ribs down, belt tight.
Sit between your knees, not behind them. Elbows track inside the knees at the bottom.
Drive through the whole foot — not just the heel — on the way up.

Primary squat-pattern movement for home gym and dumbbell-only setups. Works at any rep range: sets of 5–6 at a heavy DB for strength development; sets of 10–15 at moderate load for hypertrophy or metabolic work. A reliable 1.25× BW squat proxy when barbell is unavailable — test with the heaviest available dumbbell for 8 clean reps. Pairs well with Romanian deadlift in the same session; keep total compound sets ≤ 8 if pairing.
Bodyweight squat × 10 (pause 2 sec at bottom), then light DB goblet squat × 8, then working weight.
Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders. Toes tucked.
Body forms a straight line from head to heels — do not let hips sag or pike up.
Squeeze glutes and abs simultaneously. Breathe normally.
If form breaks before the target duration, stop and rest — do not grind through bad reps.

Use for core work in a full-body session when time is limited. Duration-based: build from 20–30 sec holds toward 60 sec. Once 3 × 60 sec is easy, progress to ab-wheel rollout or dead bug for greater anti-extension challenge. One plank set = one core set in session logs. Carries and unilateral work (split squat, single-arm row) also accumulate core volume indirectly — count those in their primary pattern only.
No specific warm-up needed. Can be placed at the end of any session or between compound sets as active rest.
Dead hang start — shoulders fully elevated, arms straight. Do not kip or swing.
Initiate by depressing the scapula (shoulders down and back) before pulling.
Pull elbows toward your back pockets, not just down. Drive the chest toward the bar.
Chin clears the bar at the top. Control the descent — 2–3 seconds down.
Full extension at the bottom before the next rep. No half-rep bunny hops.

The pull goal for Tier 30–39 is 10 unbroken pull-ups (from dead hang). Progress by adding one rep every 1–2 weeks, or by adding load (weight vest or dumbbell between feet) once 8+ clean reps are consistent. Work sets of 3–5 reps (2 reps short of failure) outperform grinding sets to failure for long-term development. If current max is < 5, use band-assisted-pull-up as the primary movement and accumulate volume there first. Never count partial reps toward the goal.
Dead hang × 20 sec, scapular pulls × 5 (no elbow bend), then 2–3 easy warm-up reps.
Hands slightly wider than shoulder-width. Elbows track at ~45 degrees — not flared out.
Body forms a rigid plank from head to heels — squeeze glutes and abs before descending.
Chest touches or nearly touches the floor at the bottom. Do not short-rep.
Press up explosively; control the descent for 2 seconds.
For easier variation: hands elevated on a surface reduces load. For harder: feet elevated.

The Tier 30–39 push goal is 15 unbroken full push-ups (chest to floor, full extension). Progress by tracking max unbroken reps each week and aiming to add 1–2 reps per week. When current max is ≥ 12, begin adding resistance (weight vest, plate on back) to continue progression. Counts as a push-pattern set. Push-ups and dumbbell bench press target the same pattern — use them interchangeably or combine in the same session without doubling the push volume beyond the weekly target.
5 slow-tempo push-ups (3 sec down, 1 sec pause) before working sets.
